        INPUT:
        1. The nominal income threshold above which higher indebtedness (60 percent DSTI instead of 50 percent) is
allowed is increased from HUF 600 000 to HUF 800 000 (approx. form EUR 1 520 to EUR 2 030).

The so-called de minimis limits of the regulation above which it should be applied will be increased. Currently the regulation is not applicable for the first loan of borrowers below HUF 450 000, and in case of credit lines and credit cards, once in three years, the credit line could be increased by th
2. With the current amendment the MNB has decided to repeal the age limit of 41 years for the 90% LTV limit for
first-time home buyers, effective from 2 September 2025. 

Additionally, starting in December 2025, first-time homebuyers who qualify for the higher LTV limit will need to be identified by lenders only through property registry queries.
3. Hrvatska Narodna Banka enforced a maturity limit: 
- 30 years for housing loans and non-housing loans secured by real estate collateral
- 10 years for other non-housing loans
4. On 1 July 2025, the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) transitioned the legally binding 90% Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit, initially introduced on 29 June 2022, to a non-binding measure while maintaining the same limit.
5. Hrvatska Narodna Banka enforced a 90% LTV limit with up to 20% of new loans allowed to exceed this limit. Of these exemptions, at least 75% of loans must be granted to consumers purchasing their primary residence.
6. Hrvatska Narodna Banka enforced a DSTI limit: 
- 45% for housing loans, with up to 20% of new loans allowed to exceed this limit. Of these exemptions, at least 75% must be granted to the consumers purchasing their primary residence
- 40% for non-housing loans, with up to 10% of new loans allowed to exceed this limit
7. On 1 July 2025, the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) transitioned the legally binding maturity 35 years limit, initially introduced on 29 June 2022, to a non-binding measure while maintaining the same limit.
8. On 1 July 2025, the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) transitioned the legally binding 40% debt service-to-income (DSTI) limit, initially introduced on 29 June 2022, to a non-binding measure while maintaining the same limit.
9. When assessing a customer’s debt-service ability lenders must ensure that the customer have sufficient funds to cover regular expenses after an interest rate increase of 3 percentage points. With fixed interest rate, the stress test applies to 
remaining debt according to the down-payment plan at 
the end of the fixed interest rate period, expected growth 
in income and costs may be taken into account.
10. Bank of Greece has activated a binding loan to value at origination (LTV-O) cap of 90% for first time buyers, and of 80% for second and subsequent time buyers. Each quarter, 10% of the total number of new loans approved can be exempt.
